scheme_name: Workers for Class 9th to 12th Through National Scholarship (JKBOCWWB)
description:
The Workers for Class 9th to 12th Through National Scholarship scheme is an initiative launched by the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (JKBOCWWB).

This scheme was established to provide financial assistance to the children of registered construction workers in Jammu and Kashmir.

The scheme was officially launched on March 1, 2021.

The primary objective of this scholarship program is to ensure that children of construction workers have access to quality education.

The scheme aims to support students from Class 9 to Class 12.

The measurable target of the scheme is to provide scholarships to at least 5,000 students annually.

The scholarship amount is set at INR 20,000 per year for each eligible student.

This financial assistance is intended to cover various educational expenses such as tuition fees, books, and other necessary materials.

To be eligible for this scholarship, applicants must be children of registered construction workers.

The construction worker must be registered with the JKBOCWWB.

The age limit for the students applying for this scholarship is between 14 to 18 years.

This means that students must be in Class 9 to Class 12 to qualify.

The income criteria for the registered construction worker is that their annual income should not exceed INR 8 lakh.

This ensures that the benefits of the scheme reach those who are in genuine need of financial support.

The application process for this scholarship involves several specific steps.

First, the applicant must obtain the application form from the official JKBOCWWB website or their local office.

The application form must be filled out completely and accurately.

Required documents include a copy of the construction worker's registration certificate.

Additionally, a copy of the student's birth certificate is necessary to verify age.

The applicant must also provide proof of the student's enrollment in a recognized school.

This can include a school admission letter or a current school ID.

Once the application form and documents are ready, they must be submitted to the nearest JKBOCWWB office.

The submission can be done in person or through a designated online portal.

After submission, the applications will be reviewed by the board.

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of application submission.

Once approved, the scholarship amount will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the registered construction worker.

The disbursement is usually done in one installment at the beginning of the academic year.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

For any queries or assistance, individuals can contact the JKBOCWWB office at their regional centers.

The contact details for the JKBOCWWB can be found on their official website.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to uplift the socio-economic status of construction workers and their families.

It aims to reduce dropout rates among children of construction workers.

By providing financial support, the scheme encourages students to continue their education.

The scholarship is renewable each year as long as the student maintains satisfactory academic performance.

Students must achieve a minimum of 40% marks in their previous academic year to remain eligible for renewal.

This ensures that the scholarship is awarded to students who are committed to their education.

The JKBOCWWB also conducts awareness programs to inform construction workers about the benefits of this scholarship.

These programs are held in various districts across Jammu and Kashmir.

The board collaborates with local schools to facilitate the application process for students.

This partnership aims to streamline the scholarship application and disbursement process.

The scheme has been well-received by the construction worker community.

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates that the financial assistance has significantly alleviated educational expenses.

Many parents have reported that the scholarship has allowed their children to pursue higher education.

The JKBOCWWB has set up a dedicated helpline for any inquiries related to the scholarship.

This helpline operates from Monday to Friday during business hours.

The board also provides updates on the scholarship scheme through social media platforms.

This ensures that information is disseminated widely and reaches all potential beneficiaries.

The impact of the scheme is being monitored through regular assessments.

These assessments help in understanding the effectiveness of the scholarship in improving educational outcomes.

The JKBOCWWB is committed to enhancing the welfare of construction workers and their families.

The scholarship scheme is a vital component of this commitment.

It reflects the government's dedication to promoting education among marginalized communities.

The government aims to create a more educated workforce in the construction sector.

This aligns with national goals of increasing literacy rates and educational attainment.

Overall, the Workers for Class 9th to 12th Through National Scholarship scheme is a significant step towards empowering the children of construction workers in Jammu and Kashmir.

It provides them with the necessary financial support to pursue their educational aspirations.

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts in ensuring that no child is left behind in the pursuit of education.

By addressing the financial barriers faced by these families, the scheme contributes to the overall development of society.

The JKBOCWWB continues to seek ways to improve and expand the scholarship program.

This includes exploring additional funding sources and partnerships with educational institutions.

The long-term goal is to create a sustainable framework for educational support for construction workers' children.

This initiative is crucial for building a brighter future for the next generation in Jammu and Kashmir.
